source.title: Catastrophic Fisher Explosion: Early Phase Fisher Matrix Impacts Generalization
source.authors: Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Devansh Arpit; Oliver Åstrand; Giancarlo Kerg; Huan Wang; Caiming Xiong; R. Socher; Kyunghyun Cho; Krzysztof J. Geras

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix; no material truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports training classification accuracy for CIFAR models under ordinary SGD, Fisher Penalty, and synthetic label noise. These results bear on V1, though the paper studies Fisher regularization and generalization rather than aiming to test the broader claim.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported training-accuracy outcomes in Tables 6, 8, and 9. Correlations between Fisher trace and test accuracy, test-accuracy comparisons, and cited findings are not training-error results for these versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training accuracies under SGD, including randomly corrupted labels and explicit regularization. These directly test V1 despite the study's focus on generalization. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but abbreviated. The authors argue that large learning rates implicitly penalize early Fisher trace, that explicitly penalizing it can improve generalization, and that Fisher Penalty suppresses memorization by slowing noisy-example learning more than clean-example learning. They acknowledge that clean-example learning also slows.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines SGD and introduces Fisher Penalty to study generalization and memorization; it does not reproduce the original studies' training-error experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy differs by model and regularization condition; for noisy labels it also differs substantially between clean and noisy subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: TinyImageNet reference runs reach 99.84% and 99.96% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can fit TinyImageNet nearly perfectly with the tested Wide ResNet and training schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Early Fisher trace predicts generalization and differs with learning rate and batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD hyperparameters influence early Fisher trace and subsequent generalization; this does not establish V5's stability-threshold behavior.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The paper studies vision tasks only. It reports final epoch accuracy for some training results and best-validation-point test metrics elsewhere; the claim's full random-label and optimizer scope is not covered.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 includes additional gradient-penalty variants (GPx, GP, GPr) with separate final training-accuracy cells. Omitted to keep the catalog focused on baseline/η∗ and Fisher Penalty conditions. Table 8 also reports Mixup and GPx clean-example results; Table 9 reports Mixup and GPx noisy-example results. They are comparator recipes rather than the principal SGD/Fisher-Penalty comparison.

untested.parts: Adam, fully random-labeled datasets, corrupted-label CIFAR-10, and controlled model-size comparisons are untested. Final training accuracies for 50% corruption are not supplied. Validation early stopping is mentioned for noisy-label experiments, but its effect on final training error is not isolated.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or measurement of spurious minima versus extra width.
No matched depth comparison of plain and residual networks or test of the stated initialization exceptions.
No initialization comparison measuring training speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate comparison against a measured initial stability threshold, catapult recovery test, or full-batch sharpness trajectory at that threshold.
No matched normalization comparison measuring training speed, stability, or learning-rate tolerance. Using Fixup or SkipInit alone does not test these comparisons.

missing.what: Final training accuracies with augmentation at optimal learning rate, η* versus FP: DenseNet/C100 98.75±0.27% versus 97.53±1.75%; SimpleCNN/C10 97.52±1.98% versus 98.94±0.08%; VGG11/C100 98.64±0.06% versus 93.06±0.01%; Wide ResNet/C100 99.97±0.01% versus 99.97±0.00%. Table 7 is not declared in rows_left_out.

CIFAR training accuracies for ResNet-26 across learning-rate and batch-size sweeps. Most runs reach approximately 99% or above. Record these as maximum training accuracies along the trajectory, averaged across seeds, with uncertainty where readable.
missing.locator: Appendix A.1, Figures 8–9; Sections 3 and I.1

record.verdict_notes: The regularization limitations qualify near-perfect fitting and are consistent with V1's explicit exception for some regularized recipes. No claim of optimization impossibility follows from finite-duration incomplete fitting. Tables 8–9 report final-epoch training accuracy; Table 3 instead reports test accuracy at the best validation point. The source inconsistently names the residual architecture across tables, prose and captions.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test random labels across the full training set, Adam, CIFAR-10 random-label training, or comparisons involving model width, early stopping, or small models as such. Its noisy-label results use 25% or 50% label noise, while separate clean-data results report final training accuracy.
